blocks.text: Scripture makes clear that there are "diversities of gifts" given by the same God beyond the five foundational ministries already discussed - {{1co 12:4,1co 12:5,1co 12:6|1 Corinthians 12:4-6}}. These include:

Supernatural power to intervene in the ordinary course of nature, counteracting natural laws when necessary - {{hb 2:3,hb 2:4|Hebrews 2:3-4}}, {{mt 17:20|Matthew 17:20}}. Some believers are divinely anointed for this office, their words, actions, and faith producing visible miracles; this gift may stand alone or complement one of the foundational ministries. Faith is the key condition - {{mk 11:22,mk 11:23,mk 11:24|Mark 11:22-24}}.

Supernatural power to heal every kind of sickness without medicine or human aid - {{mk 16:18|Mark 16:18}}, {{act 3:6|Acts 3:6}}. Some believers carry this gift without necessarily being able to preach or teach - a simple laying on of hands brings immediate recovery. It can also complement the other foundational ministries - {{act 19:11,act 19:12|Acts 19:11-12}}.

The Greek antilepsis, translated "helps" in {{1co 12:28|1 Corinthians 12:28}}, means supporter, assistant, or protector - the supernatural ability to perform practical, helpful work with grace. Deacons, deaconesses, ushers, sanctuary keepers, technical crews, drivers, and medical practitioners all fall under this gift - {{rm 16:3,rm 16:9|Romans 16:3, 9}}, {{1co 16:16|1 Corinthians 16:16}}. These are the "Aarons" and "Hurs" who steady the hands of Moses, the pastor - {{ex 17:10,ex 17:11,ex 17:12,ex 17:13|Exodus 17:10-13}}. Their contribution to the body of Christ should never be underestimated; they also care for the poor and needy, as Dorcas and Phoebe did - {{act 9:36,act 9:37,act 9:38,act 9:39|Acts 9:36-39}}, {{rm 16:1,rm 16:2|Romans 16:1-2}}. Those gifted in giving and showing mercy can also be grouped here - {{rm 12:7,rm 12:8|Romans 12:7-8}}.

The supernatural ability to organise, administer, and coordinate the affairs of a local church. The Greek kubernesis means steering or pilotage - the divine responsibility for guiding and administering the church - {{tt 1:4,tt 1:5|Titus 1:4-5}}. This isn't about the power to rule, but the gift of extraordinary wisdom, knowledge, and discernment needed to guide a church through its affairs and problems. No church grows beyond a certain point without individuals carrying this gift.

{{rm 12:8|Romans 12:8}} names this divine ability to exhort - from the Greek parakaleo, "to call aside" or "to appeal by way of entreaty and comfort." People like Barnabas, called "son of consolation", are supernaturally gifted to counsel and strengthen others for the journey of life. Trained counsellors and gospel musicians often exhibit this gift too; it can also be listed under the ministry of prophets.
